pr_title: Introduce a WinRT utils library and "checked resources"
pr_body:
This commit introduces a C++/WinRT utility library and moves
ScopedResourceLoader into it. I decided to get uppity and introduce
something I like to call "checked resources." The idea is that every
resource reference from a library is knowable at compile time, and we
should be able to statically ensure that all resources exist.

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #2146
* [x] CLA
* [ ] Tests added/passed
* [ ] Requires documentation to be updated
* [x] I've discussed this with core contributors already.

## Details

This is a system that lets us immediately failfast (on launch) when a
library makes a static reference to a resource that doesn't exist at
runtime.

It exposes two new (preprocessor) APIs:
* `RS_(wchar_t)`: loads a localizable string resource by name.
* `USES_RESOURCE(wchar_t)`: marks a resource key as used, but is intended
  for loading images or passing static resource keys as parameters to
  functions that will look them up later.

Resource checking relies on diligent use of `USES_RESOURCE()` and `RS_()`
(which uses `USES_RESOURCE`), but can make sure we don't ship something
that'll blow up at runtime.

It works like this:

**IN DEBUG MODE**
- All resource names referenced through `USES_RESOURCE()` are emitted
  alongside their referencing filenames and line numbers into a static
  section of the binary.
  That section is named `.util$res$m`.

- We emit two sentinel values into two different sections, `.util$res$a`
  and `.util$res$z`.

- The linker sorts all sections alphabetically before crushing them
  together into the final binary.

- When we first construct a library's scoped resource loader, we
  iterate over every resource reference between `$a` and `$z` and check
  residency.

**IN RELEASE MODE**
- All checked resource code is compiled out.

Fixes #2146.

Macros are the only way to do something this cool, incidentally.

## Validation Steps Performed
Made references to a bunch of bad resources, tried to break it a lot.

It looks like this when it fails:

### App.cpp
```
36  static const std::array<std::wstring_view, 2> settingsLoadErrorsLabels {
37      USES_RESOURCE(L"NoProfilesText"),
38      USES_RESOURCE(L"AllProfilesHiddenText_HA_JUST_KIDDING")
39  };
```

```
WinRTUtils\LibraryResources.cpp(68)\TerminalApp.dll:
    FailFast(1) tid(1034) 8000FFFF Catastrophic failure
    Msg:[Resource AllProfilesHiddenText_HA_JUST_KIDDING not found in
      scope TerminalApp/Resources (App.cpp:38)] [EnsureAllResourcesArePresent]
```
pr_comments: Also (!!!) `USES_RESOURCE` works in a static context like settingsLoadErrorLabels, which was an awesome surprise.
I think our builds will be fine :)

If you attempt to use a dynamic value in `RS_` or `USES_RESOURCE`, you get this error:

```
error C3493: 'x' cannot be implicitly captured because no default capture
  mode has been specified
```

I think it's the best we can do for this diagnostic.
The CI is failing because every project referenced by UnitTests_TerminalApp is being built twice.

issue_context.title: Produce a winrt-specific types library to hold some of our WinRT helpers without cluttering conhost
issue_context.body:
* Things like `ScopedResourceLoader` would go in there.
   * Related: #2142, localizing the azure connection, other cross-project localization issues
* It would provide a central place for the cppwinrt_utils header and friends to live (and an include path :P)

review_comments: Lets maybe add a note here that this is load-bearing. I foresee us definitely forgetting that in some future where we add another binary.
It'll actually fail to link if you leave it out

So for my own checking, this _could_ be `RS_(titleKey)`, but since the caller already passed in the param with `USES_RESOURCE()`, we're just skipping doing a redundant `USES_RESOURCE` here, right?

Or is there other static-analysis magic here that I'm missing?
Nah, this can't be `RS_` -- RS will try to emit a static resource reference into that binary segment, but it can't because this is not a static constant value.
i think this will fail at compile time, but in an unclear way

I'm not sure I love `RS_` as the macro, because I'd think for someone who's _not_ familiar with the code, there's _no_ indication what it's really doing. (I don't have a better suggestion at this time though)
yeah, i don't love it either.. it's sorta modelled after other localization libraries (which use `_()` or `S_()` or `L_()`)

How fragile is this? Is there any chance something else might get compiled at `.util$res$...` such that it would make this all explode? (Merely an informative question, I have a very limited understanding of how the c++ linker works in this regard)

Not fragile. All the section names in common use are very well-documented and unchanging.

ATL uses this trick, as does the compiler, with other special section names. We could namespace ours better, but it'll just make it more unlikely that it collides.
if `g_WinRTUtilsLibraryResourceScope` isn't ever set, will this explode?
if it's not set it won't link at all
Should this one be in `LibraryIncludes.h`? Or is it too sensitive to the include order?

I believe this one has a sensitive include order.. but i am not sure.
We may also not want to include it in LibraryIncludes for _all conhost stuff_
conhost, it might actually be warranted for the TSF stuff that is COMish. but its fine.
